config.title: Build delayed job execution API

intro.title: Build delayed job execution API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a delayed job execution API using Node.js. This API will allow you to schedule tasks to run after a specified delay, simulating a basic job queue system. You'll learn how to use JavaScript's setTimeout function to handle asynchronous delays and manage job state. The lesson will involve creating HTTP endpoints to submit jobs, track their status, and execute them at the right time. By the end, you'll have a working API that demonstrates core concepts of asynchronous programming and job scheduling in a backend environment.
intro.usecase: Delayed job execution is essential for handling time-sensitive operations in production applications. For example, e-commerce platforms use delayed jobs to send order confirmation emails 30 minutes after purchase, or to automatically cancel unpaid orders after 24 hours. Social media platforms schedule content publishing for optimal engagement times, while subscription services process billing renewals at specific intervals. Developers implement these patterns to create responsive user experiences where long-running tasks don't block immediate interactions, ensuring systems remain performant under load.

objectives: Construct a Node.js server with Express to handle HTTP requests
Implement a job queue using an in-memory array for storing delayed tasks
Configure route handlers to accept job creation requests with delay parameters
Initialize a background worker process to check and execute pending jobs
Manipulate job statuses (pending, processing, completed) throughout their lifecycle
Integrate job cancellation functionality with proper error handling
Apply setTimeout for delayed execution based on user-specified intervals
